sources.inspection: Original PDF text extracted and read
findings: Describes Pataras dealing in silk and cotton yarn, necklace stringing, reeled yarn, hand-spun tussar and silk, tie-and-dye borders, applique designs and weaving supplements.

limits: District summary, not dated household fieldwork or community founding evidence.
PDF upload filename is not an established publication year.

sources.title: Edgar Thurston and K. Rangachari, Castes and Tribes of Southern India, Volume VI (1909)
sources.inspection: Original book transcription inspected, including printed-page markers
findings: Oriya Patrā entry distinguishes silk waist-thread and tassel manufacture from silk-cloth weaving.
Names Mahānāyako as cloth-weaving section head, with Bēhara and Bhollobaya officers; the other section has Sēnāpati assisted by Dhanapati.
A separately described Telugu Patrā population in Cuddapah and Kurnool has hunting and cultivation associations. That account is not Odisha Patara evidence.
limits: Colonial classification is a dated outside description, not current community authority.
Do not infer caste from listed surnames, preserve discrimination as historical only if relevant, and omit irrelevant child-marriage prescriptions.
Correct printed locator is 177; a later NCBC search snippet says 176, but direct page markers support 177.
No proven founding event or date.

sources.title: Arunika Mohapatra, Learning the ropes of the festival, Times of India, 23 June 2017
sources.locator: article body, particularly paragraphs identifying pataras and interview with Santosh Kumar Patra; web lines 151–161
sources.inspection: Full original article opened and read
findings: Reporting explicitly calls the Puri sevayats pataras; connection does not depend on the interviewed person’s surname.
Describes silk Bijaya Dori for pahandi, made with silk from Nuapatna; interviewee Santosh Kumar Patra describes hand preparation and measurements estimated by eye.
Reports fathers and grandfathers training young men. Scope is these temple servitors in 2017.
Explicitly distinguishes the silk procession ropes from chariot-pulling ropes acquired from Odisha Coir Board.
limits: Named, dated temple service reporting does not identify all Patara community members as servitors.
No founding date follows from family training.
Do not reproduce the claim that estimates never go wrong as objective verification.
Photo rights unverified; no reuse recommended.

sources.title: Bratati Baral, Mahabahu to adorn Rakhi as servitors put finishing touches on sacred threads, Prameya News, 27 August 2026
sources.locator: Traditional Crafting Process section, web lines 25–33; identification lines 18–23
sources.inspection: Full original article opened and read independently
findings: Explicitly names Patara Bisoi servitors, and quotes Santosh Kumar Patra about family service.
Describes Vasunga silk supplied by temple administration, dyeing, sun drying, shaping into circular layers and use of wooden comb to arrange five layers.
Links preparation to Gamha Purnima and says the work is done at servitors’ homes.
limits: Dated reporting of one temple service, not an exhaustive account of the community.
Specific tools and methods differ from the 2017 rope account because the objects differ; do not imply contradiction or combine into one technique.
No basis for measuring antiquity of current procedure.
Photo rights not verified; no reuse.
